title: The atom
prompt: a Bohr-style atom model on a tabletop stand with a small element dial: pick hydrogen, helium, carbon or neon and the nucleus and electron shells rebuild with the right protons, neutrons and electrons; fire a photon to kick an electron up a shell, then watch it fall back and emit a photon whose colour matches the energy gap; see-through shows the nucleus with protons and neutrons, the shell energy levels and the spectral lines on a small spectroscope strip

title: Molecules and bonds
prompt: a ball-and-stick molecule kit on a bench: switch between water, carbon dioxide, methane and ammonia, show the bond angles as little protractor arcs, make the molecule vibrate and rotate, and toggle polarity arrows that show where electrons sit; see-through swaps to the electron-cloud view with shared electron pairs and lone pairs

title: Gas laws
prompt: a glass cylinder of gas with a weighted piston, a thermometer, a pressure gauge and a bunsen burner under it: push the piston down and watch pressure rise as volume falls, light the burner and watch the molecules speed up and the piston rise, pump in more gas; molecules visibly bounce off the walls and piston; stats show P, V, T and PV/T staying constant

title: Newton's three laws
prompt: a low-friction air track with a cart, a spring plunger, a stack of add-on masses and a second cart: push with the plunger and see the force arrow, acceleration and velocity readouts, add a mass to show the same push giving less acceleration, let the two carts collide to show equal and opposite force arrows, switch friction on so the cart slows; see-through shows the air holes in the track, the spring in the plunger and a force diagram

title: Galileo's drop
prompt: a tall glass vacuum tube with a feather and a steel ball held at the top by a release catch, a vacuum pump on the side and a stopwatch: drop them in air and the feather lags, pump the air out and drop again so they fall together, replay in slow motion with a distance ruler showing the squares pattern 1, 4, 9; see-through shows the pump piston, valves and the release mechanism

title: The pendulum
prompt: a pendulum on a wooden frame with an adjustable string length, swappable bobs and a period counter: start it swinging, shorten or lengthen the string to change the period, swap a heavy bob for a light one to show the period does not change, swing it wider; see-through shows the tension and gravity force arrows, the velocity arrow and a small energy bar trading kinetic for potential

title: Special relativity
prompt: a toy train on a straight track carrying a light clock (a photon bouncing between two mirrors) past a platform with an identical clock: set the train speed to 0, half or nine tenths of light speed, start both clocks and watch the train's photon trace a longer zigzag path so its clock ticks slower, toggle length contraction to see the train squash; stats show the Lorentz factor and both clock readings

title: Maxwell's electromagnetic wave
prompt: a transmitting antenna fed by an oscillator, open air, and a receiving antenna wired to a small lamp: transmit and watch the electric field arrows and the perpendicular magnetic field arrows ripple outward as a wave, change the frequency from radio through microwave to visible and see wavelength change and the colour band on a spectrum strip, move the receiver to a node; see-through shows electrons sloshing in the antenna rods and the current in the receiver lighting the lamp

title: Faraday's induction
prompt: a coil of copper wire on a cardboard tube wired to a centre-zero galvanometer, with a bar magnet on a slider: push the magnet in and the needle kicks one way, pull it out and it kicks the other, push faster for a bigger kick, add more turns to the coil; see-through shows the magnetic field lines threading the coil and the induced current direction as moving dots in the wire

title: The double-slit experiment
prompt: a laser on an optical bench, a plate with two slits and a screen with a photographic strip: fire single photons one at a time and watch dots build up into interference fringes, open the full beam to show the bright and dark bands at once, cover one slit so the fringes vanish into a single blob, place a detector at a slit so the pattern collapses to two lumps; see-through shows the wavefronts spreading from both slits and where they add or cancel

title: The photoelectric effect
prompt: a vacuum tube with a metal plate and a collector wired to an ammeter and a variable voltage, lit by a lamp with a colour wheel: pick red, green, blue or ultraviolet light and only light above the threshold knocks electrons out, turn the brightness up to get more electrons but no faster ones, raise the stopping voltage until the current drops to zero; stats show photon energy, work function and electron kinetic energy

title: Rutherford's gold foil
prompt: a lead box with a radium source firing alpha particles at a gold foil inside a ring-shaped zinc sulphide screen with a microscope on a swinging arm: fire alphas and most pass straight through with faint flashes, a few deflect and very rarely one bounces back, swing the microscope round the ring to count flashes, toggle the plum-pudding prediction overlay; see-through zooms the foil to show mostly empty atoms with tiny dense nuclei doing the scattering

title: The Cavendish experiment
prompt: a torsion balance in a glass case: a light rod with two small lead balls hanging from a thin wire, two large lead balls on a swinging frame outside, a lamp and mirror throwing a light spot onto a scale: swing the big balls to one side and watch the rod twist very slowly toward them and the light spot creep along the scale, swing them to the other side, release and watch the slow oscillation; stats show the tiny force and the computed G

title: Prism and lenses
prompt: an optical bench with a white lamp, a glass prism on a turntable and a screen, plus a converging and a diverging lens in holders: rotate the prism to split white light into a spectrum on the screen, swap in the converging lens and slide a candle object to see a real inverted image focus, swap in the diverging lens to see a virtual image, trace the rays; see-through shows the ray paths bending at each glass surface with refraction angles

title: A simple circuit
prompt: a breadboard with a battery pack, a switch, two bulbs, a resistor dial and an ammeter and voltmeter: close the switch and the bulb lights, add the second bulb in series so both dim, rewire it in parallel so both stay bright, turn the resistor dial; see-through shows electrons as moving dots along the wires and a water-pipe analogy pressure arrow at the battery; stats show V, I and R with Ohm's law

title: Standing waves
prompt: a long string between a mechanical vibrator and a pulley with hanging weights, a frequency dial and a strobe lamp: start the vibrator and step the frequency through the first, second and third harmonics to see one, two and three loops with nodes and antinodes, add weight to raise the tension, flip on the strobe to freeze the motion; see-through shows the two travelling waves adding to make the standing wave

title: A chemical reaction
prompt: a sealed glass reaction chamber with a spark plug, a bond-energy meter and molecule-count display, filled with methane and oxygen molecules bumping around: press spark and watch bonds break and reform into carbon dioxide and water with a flash and heat, replay in slow motion to see a single collision break and make bonds, reset the gas, toggle a catalyst surface that makes it go at lower temperature; see-through shows the energy diagram with the activation hump

title: Electrolysis of water
prompt: a Hofmann voltameter: a glass U-tube with two platinum electrodes, two collecting tubes with taps and a battery with a switch: switch on and watch bubbles rise with twice as much hydrogen as oxygen collecting, open a tap and test the hydrogen with a lit splint for a pop, test the oxygen with a glowing splint that flares, swap the battery polarity; see-through shows water molecules splitting and ions drifting to each electrode

title: Acid-base titration
prompt: a burette on a stand over a conical flask on a magnetic stirrer with a pH meter and indicator: add base drop by drop from the burette, swirl, watch the pH creep then jump and the indicator flip from colourless to pink at the endpoint, overshoot and go purple, reset; see-through shows hydrogen and hydroxide ions in the flask neutralising into water and a live pH-against-volume curve

title: States of matter
prompt: a beaker of ice on a hot plate with a thermometer and a lid with a weight on it: heat so the ice melts, the water warms and then boils with the temperature pausing at each phase change, cool it back down, press the lid to raise pressure and shift the boiling point; see-through shows a zoomed box of molecules locked in a lattice, then jostling, then flying free, with a heating curve plot

title: A battery (Daniell cell)
prompt: a Daniell cell: a zinc strip in zinc sulphate and a copper strip in copper sulphate, joined by a salt bridge, wired through a switch to a small bulb and voltmeter: close the switch and the bulb lights, watch the zinc strip thin and the copper strip thicken over fast time, swap the zinc for magnesium to raise the voltage, remove the salt bridge and the bulb dies; see-through shows electrons going round the wire and ions crossing the bridge

title: Distillation
prompt: a round flask of salty or alcoholic water on a heater, a thermometer at the neck, a Liebig condenser with cooling water hoses and a collecting flask: heat until the vapour reaches the condenser and drips of pure liquid collect, switch between salt water and wine to see the different boiling temperatures, turn off the cooling water so vapour escapes; see-through shows molecules leaving the hot liquid, cooling in the inner tube and the counterflow of cold water

title: The living cell
prompt: an animal cell as a cutaway globe on a stand: switch on the organelle labels one group at a time, follow a protein being made as DNA in the nucleus is read, mRNA leaves, a ribosome on the rough ER builds the protein and a vesicle carries it to the membrane, run mitosis so chromosomes line up and the cell pinches in two; see-through shows the membrane with its channel proteins and the cytoskeleton

title: DNA replication
prompt: a short double helix held on a stand like a model kit: unzip it with helicase, watch polymerase run along each strand adding matching bases from a tray of A, T, C, G blocks, finish with two identical helices, rewind; see-through shows base pairs as colour-matched puzzle pieces with hydrogen bonds and the sugar-phosphate backbone

title: The heart
prompt: a human heart on a stand with the big vessels, a stethoscope and a heart-rate dial: beat once slowly and follow blood into the right atrium, through the valve to the ventricle, out to the lungs, back into the left side and out the aorta, raise the rate as if exercising, hold the valves open to show backflow; see-through shows the four chambers, the valve flaps opening and shutting and the pacemaker signal spreading

title: Photosynthesis
prompt: a potted leafy plant under a desk lamp inside a glass bell jar with a carbon dioxide meter and an oxygen bubble counter: switch on the lamp and watch carbon dioxide molecules enter the leaf pores, water rise through the stem and oxygen bubbles leave, dim or brighten the lamp to change the rate, change the lamp colour to green so it nearly stops; see-through shows a leaf cross-section with stomata, veins and chloroplasts turning light into sugar

title: The neuron
prompt: a neuron laid out on a board: dendrites, cell body, a long axon with myelin sleeves, and a synapse onto a second neuron, with a voltage trace meter: poke the dendrite and if the stimulus is strong enough an action potential races down the axon as a wave of sodium going in and potassium coming out, jumping between myelin gaps, then neurotransmitter vesicles pop across the synapse; try a weak stimulus that fails, add a blocker drug at the synapse

title: Sun, Earth and Moon
prompt: a brass orrery of the Sun, Earth and Moon on geared arms with a lamp in the Sun: run a month and watch the Moon's phases on a small phase dial, step to a solar eclipse with the Moon's shadow falling on Earth, step to a lunar eclipse with the Moon in Earth's shadow, tilt the Moon's orbit to show why eclipses are rare; see-through shows the gear train and the shadow cones

title: The seasons
prompt: a tilted globe of Earth on a circular track round a lamp Sun, with a little pin at one latitude and a sun-angle and day-length readout: advance through the four seasons and watch the tilt stay fixed while the lit half shifts, show the midday sun angle at the pin, show the day and night length, straighten the tilt to kill the seasons; see-through shows the sunlight as parallel rays and the spread of energy over the ground

title: A reflecting telescope
prompt: a Newtonian reflecting telescope on a tripod pointed at a small moon on the wall, with a focuser knob and eyepiece: turn the focuser to bring the moon sharp in a little eyepiece view, swap eyepieces to change magnification, open the tube to show the curved primary mirror, the flat secondary and the light path; see-through traces the light rays from the moon bouncing off both mirrors into the eye

title: Pythagoras in water
prompt: a wooden right triangle with glass squares built on each side, the two smaller ones full of blue water, mounted on a pivot: flip the whole thing and watch the water from the two small squares pour exactly into the big square on the hypotenuse, flip back, change the triangle's shape by sliding a corner and the squares resize; see-through shows the area formulas and the four congruent triangles proof overlay

title: Fourier's epicycles
prompt: a drawing machine of linked rotating arms (epicycles) with a pen on the last one tracing onto a moving paper strip: run with one arm to draw a sine wave, add harmonics one at a time and watch the trace sharpen toward a square wave, switch the target shape to a sawtooth, slow down to see each circle's contribution; see-through shows the gear ratios driving each arm and the frequency bars
